preferences.description: I want you to state the time complexity BEFORE writing any code.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Wait, state the time complexity first before writing code.

preferences.description: I dislike list comprehensions with more than one nested for clause; use a regular loop instead.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: That nested comprehension is unreadable - rewrite it as a plain loop.

preferences.description: I want iterative solutions over recursive ones whenever iteration is possible, even when recursion is shorter.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Don't use recursion here - rewrite iteratively.

preferences.description: Skip the preamble. Don't restate the problem before answering.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Cut the intro, go straight to the solution.

preferences.description: Before solving, always enumerate 2-3 edge cases that the solution will handle.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: What edge cases are you covering? List them first.

preferences.description: Prefer stdlib over third-party packages; only import third-party if stdlib is truly insufficient.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: No third-party deps if stdlib can do it.

preferences.description: I want type hints on every function signature.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Add type hints to the signatures.

preferences.description: Keep explanations under 3 sentences unless I explicitly ask for more detail.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Too much explanation - keep it to ~3 sentences.

preferences.description: Never use `print` for debugging; use `logging` instead.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Don't use print for debugging - use logging.

preferences.description: If input validation is needed, do it at the top of the function with explicit guards, not with try/except.
preferences.expected_correction_trigger: Use explicit guards, not try/except, for input validation.
